newsitem.title: USA: Thomson says Vanguard suit without merit.
newsitem.headline: Thomson says Vanguard suit without merit.

text.p: Thomson Publishing Corp, a unit of Thomson Corp, said Monday a lawsuit filed by the Vanguard Group alleging mistakes in calculating Thomson's municipal futures index is "without merit."

Michael Harris, vice president and general counsel at Thomson, said in a telephone interview that Thomson's Bond Buyer unit "prepares the index in accordance with rules established by the Chicago Board of Trade."
"We followed (the Board of Trade rules), and did them accordingly, and we think the lawsuit is entirely without merit," Harris said.
Vanguard on May 5 filed a lawsuit in U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois naming Thomson and six municipal bond brokers as defendants.
The lawsuit alleges that seven of Vanguard's municipal bond funds lost at least $3.25 million because the Bond Buyer mispriced the contract underlying the municipal bond futures contract.

The lawsuit said the errors occurred on Dec. 19, 1995, when the Federal Reserve lowered short-term interest rates 25 basis points on the same day the muni futures contract settled. Vanguard, which held 3,420 contracts that day, alleges that the index underlying the contract did not reflect the muni market's sharp reaction to the Fed move until a day later, when the contract had already expired.
